learned_from_review.summary: Reviewer + critic findings from the first pass (2026-06-30). Captured here so future plans can apply the same validation discipline without re-discovering the issues.

findings.title: Never assume an external endpoint is reachable - prove it with a BLOCKER preflight before building on top
findings.lesson: The original plan assumed /signoz/ws/logs/v5/{orgId} works against live SigNoz without verification. If the WS contract is wrong or Caddy does not route correctly, every downstream task (logsLiveTail.ts, w3-t2 wire, etc.) wastes weeks. Future plans that depend on any external service MUST include a verification script (curl / openssl / kafkacat / mongosh) that exits non-zero on failure with a SPECIFIC remediation message keyed off the failure mode (connection refused vs 404 vs 502 vs 401).

findings.title: Offset-based virtualization is fragile when row content varies - use overlay UI for content expansion
findings.lesson: A fixed-row-height + overscan virtualization breaks the moment any row's content exceeds the fixed height (offset math becomes wrong for every subsequent row). The fix is to render content expansion as an absolutely-positioned overlay (anchored to the row's viewport position, dismissable on Esc / backdrop click / X button) rather than inline row expansion. The overlay sits in its own stacking context and does not affect the table's virtualization math. Tests should explicitly assert the table's height is invariant under expand-collapse cycles.
findings.applied_in: w2-t1 (split into LogRow + LogTable + JsonDrawer.svelte overlay)

findings.title: Lock state-machine enums in the plan - implementers should not have to guess
findings.lesson: When a component renders state from a store (status pill, connection indicator, retry counter), the plan should specify the EXACT enum the implementer should use. The original plan said 'Live / Reconnecting / Live unavailable' (3 strings, vague semantics); the fix is to enumerate all 5 states explicitly: 'idle' | 'connecting' | 'open' | 'reconnecting' | 'closed'. TypeScript string literal unions over enums (better tree-shaking and matches the codebase's style).

findings.title: Hard-coded URLs in plans get duplicated - centralise into a tiny module at first use
findings.lesson: When a plan introduces a new hard-coded URL constant (IP, port, host), put it in a small typed module (frontend/src/admin/lib/{name}.ts) at the FIRST task that uses it, not later. The plan should explicitly call out the module so downstream tasks import from it instead of re-hard-coding. Saves a future grep-and-replace when the URL changes.

findings.title: DAG summary numbers must match reality - fix the count before review #2
findings.lesson: The first plan reported wave_1_task_count: 4 and total_dependencies: 8, both wildly wrong (actual: 15 tasks, 23 edges). Fix the summary numbers before sending the plan to review - a wrong DAG metric destroys reviewer trust. The 'Don't fix every math reference' rule means fix the two headline numbers (task_count, dep_count) and let downstream numbers sort themselves out.

findings.title: conflicts_with entries only make sense within the same wave - drop cross-wave noise
findings.lesson: Wave ordering already enforces serial execution across waves. conflicts_with entries that span different waves are noise - they cannot trigger because the downstream wave cannot start until the upstream wave is done. Keep conflicts_with only for true intra-wave resource contention (e.g. two tasks both writing to the same file with no merge strategy).

findings.title: YAGNI vs full enterprise solution - user request wins
findings.lesson: A critic suggested cutting Copy-as-cURL and Saved Views for YAGNI. Disagree - the user explicitly asked for a full enterprise solution. Small-LOC features (cURL = 20 LOC, saved views = 60 LOC) that provide disproportionate operator value should be KEPT when explicitly requested. Document the judgement so future plans do not re-litigate the cut.
findings.applied_in: Both features kept - Copy-as-cURL in w4-t3, Saved Views in w1-t4

findings.title: Caddyfile conditional skip is fail-open - document the operational gap explicitly
findings.lesson: The signoz_mcp role is conditional in the Caddyfile template - if /etc/ircfiber/signoz-mcp/.api_key is missing on first run, the /signoz/* route block is skipped (no startup error, just no proxy). This is a fail-open configuration that surfaces as a silent 404 in production. The plan must explicitly call out this gap (in relevant_context + pre_mortem) so operators know to run signoz_mcp first.
findings.applied_in: Updated relevant_context.vite_dev_proxy_gap + added pre_mortem failure mode

prior_failed_iframe_attempts.title: feat(deploy): admin logs routed through SigNoz via Caddy header injection
prior_failed_iframe_attempts.intent: Iframe SigNoz UI at /signoz/logs; Caddy injects SIGNOZ-API-KEY on iframe document and absolute /api/v1/... requests.
prior_failed_iframe_attempts.outcome: Initial deployment; SigNoz UI bootstraps but immediately renders the cloud-icon error page because the React bundle requires a session JWT.

prior_failed_iframe_attempts.title: fix(deploy): proxy SigNoz API and asset paths from root
prior_failed_iframe_attempts.intent: Add @signoz_api (/api/v[1-3]/*) and @signoz_static (/assets/* /css/*) matchers so absolute API calls and asset bundles proxy to SigNoz.
prior_failed_iframe_attempts.outcome: Caused regression: /assets/* intercepted admin SPA bundles (admin-*.js, legacy-*.js, main-*.js, admin-*.css). SigNoz returned its SPA HTML for unmatched assets, breaking the admin app.

prior_failed_iframe_attempts.title: fix(deploy): scope SigNoz static proxy to index-* bundles
prior_failed_iframe_attempts.intent: Fix the regression in 7795a73 by scoping @signoz_static to /assets/index-* (SigNoz's hashed bundle prefix).
prior_failed_iframe_attempts.outcome: Asset collision fixed; the admin SPA loads correctly. But the underlying problem remains: SigNoz React bundle still fails to bootstrap a session JWT from the SIGNOZ-API-KEY header. The iframe still shows the cloud-icon error page.

why_iframe_unfixable: SigNoz v0.130 combined image serves a React SPA that bootstraps a session JWT in client-side state.
The session JWT is issued by /api/v2/sessions/email_password after interactive login; it cannot be replayed by a static SIGNOZ-API-KEY header.
Caddy can inject the API key but cannot fabricate a session JWT without the login flow.

Adding a Caddy-side login proxy (POST /api/v2/sessions on each iframe load) was considered but would: (a) leak the admin password into the Caddyfile, (b) hit session-rate-limits, (c) break on every SigNoz version bump when the login API contract changes.
Conclusion: replace the iframe with a native panel that uses the same /api/v1..5/* API the iframe would have used, but rendered in Svelte 5 without depending on SigNoz's React bundle.

vite_dev_proxy_gap.caddyfile_conditional_skip_risk: The /signoz/* handle_path block in deploy/roles/caddy/templates/Caddyfile.j2 is CONDITIONAL on /etc/ircfiber/signoz-mcp/.api_key existing on the host. If signoz_mcp role has not run yet (or the file was deleted), ircfiber-caddy boots successfully but /signoz/* returns 404 - no startup error, no diagnostic. This is a fail-open operational gap. Mitigation: w1-t5-deploy-assertion probes /signoz/api/v1/services and surfaces a specific remediation message ('signoz_mcp role has not run on this host - run ansible-playbook playbooks/signoz_mcp.yml'). w3-t3-caddy-ws-audit also validates the Caddyfile route block is present.
